items.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996
items.q: Sam Woodyard was his drummer, was a wonderful drummer. I loved the way he played. I do an imitation.

ctx.x: You got in on some Ellington sessions too, right?

Um hum. He did, this was the days of those ping pong recordings, you know the stereo? When stereo really became very big? And Duke did a whole thing with percussion with the big band, with his band. Sam Woodyard was his drummer, was a wonderful drummer. I loved the way he played. I do an imitation. I mean when we do Duke Ellington charts, with any big band if I’m ever working with them, I always do an imitation of Sam Woodyard playing. I’m a good mimic. Because it works. Why would I play Benny Goodman style? It…
George was kind of a protégé of Milt, wasn’t he?
